title: Task Board
description: Schema for the repo's evolving task board (task.md is the human-readable board; tasks conform to this contract). Each task is designed to be as INDEPENDENT as possible: tasks in the same `wave` have no dependency on one another and run in parallel, and `dependsOn` carries the only ordering — keep it minimal and push shared work into its own upstream task. Not zero-touch-specific; this schema outlives any one initiative. Restricted to the JSON Schema subset Claude's Structured Outputs supports, so an agent can be constrained to it when emitting a task.

schemaVersion.description: Stable schema version. Bump only on breaking changes to this contract.

id.description: Stable, unique kebab-case key (dedupe key across edits). Convention: <initiative-or-milestone>-<slug>, e.g. 'm1-config-loader', 'harness-teardown-guard'. No counters; pick a slug and check for collision before adding.

title.description: Short human-facing title (a phrase, not the id slug).

description.description: What the task does and why. Enough for someone to pick it up cold without re-deriving context.

component.description: Ownership axis — the package/area the task touches (same axis as findings.schema.json). 'wrapper' = @cdklabs/cdk-cicd-wrapper (jsii constructs). 'cli' = @cdklabs/cdk-cicd-wrapper-cli. 'shared' = spans packages. 'infra' = tooling/docs/samples/test-harness/schema. A third value, 'projen' (@cdklabs/cdk-cicd-wrapper-projen), was retired when zero-touch removed that package (D5, consolidation 3→2) — no task used it.

type.description: Work kind — drives the conventional-commit type and separates build-work from verify-work. 'spike' = time-boxed investigation with a written outcome.

wave.description: AWS-style wave planning. Tasks in the same wave have NO dependency on each other and are meant to run in parallel; ordering across waves is expressed by dependsOn. Wave 0 is foundational (runs first). Lower waves generally precede higher ones, but the real ordering constraint is dependsOn, not the number.

status.description: Lifecycle. 'blocked' means a dependency or open decision is unresolved (say which in notes). Flip in place; do not delete finished tasks (history stays visible), mark 'done' or 'wontfix'.

spec.description: Reference to the authoritative spec for this task: a repo path plus section/anchor, e.g. 'docs/design/v3-devops-experience.md #Application configuration management'. Multiple refs separated by '; '.

dependsOn.description: Ids of tasks that must be done first (the ONLY ordering signal). Keep minimal — independence is the goal. A task that many others need should be its own upstream task rather than duplicated.

acceptance.description: The verification/gate that proves the task is done — a concrete, checkable criterion (a passing test, an asserted-then-destroyed real deploy, a green `projen compat`). This repo is goal-driven: no task is 'done' without its check green.

produces.description: Concrete outputs the task creates (file paths, constructs, artifacts), so its completion is checkable and the task is self-contained.

breaking.description: True if the task changes or removes published API/behaviour (guarded by `npx projen compat`). Under the additive-before-destructive rule these wait for a major release.

owner.description: Optional assignee — a person or an agent role.

notes.description: Optional freeform: risks, assumptions, why blocked, or links to findings.json ids / decisions.
